The bithermal fatigue lives of bare Rene N4 specimens were shorter than the isothermal fatigue lives at either 760°C or 982°C when compared on an inelastic strain basis.

Both in-phase and out-of-phase bithermal fatigue life curves converged in the large strain regime and diverged in the small strain regime, with out-of-phase bithermal fatigue resulting in the shortest lives.
For isothermal fatigue at 760°C, the coated Rene N4 specimens had significantly shorter lives than the bare specimens.
The coating had no effect on the fatigue life of specimens cycled in-phase for the strain regimes tested.
For out-of-phase bithermal fatigue under large strains, the coated Rene N4 specimens had much shorter lives than the bare specimens.
Crack initiation in bare specimens fatigued at 760°C occurred at surface and near-surface micropores, transitioning from stage I to stage II cracking.
Crack initiation in bare specimens fatigued at 982°C occurred at surface micropores and oxide cracks, with only stage II cracking observed.
For coated specimens fatigued at 982°C, crack initiation occurred at internal pores rather than the surface.
During in-phase bithermal cycling, the compressive stresses caused oxide spallation which helped blunt surface cracks in the coated specimens.
The tensile stresses during out-of-phase bithermal cycling led to surface-initiated failures in the coated specimens.
The coating thickness was measured to be about 0.055 mm, but the actual increase in specimen diameter was only 0.020 mm, indicating some coating formation by diffusion into the substrate.
The Rene N4 alloy has a gamma-gamma prime microstructure, with the gamma prime occupying about 65% by volume.
The single crystal specimens exhibited significant porosity, about 0.4% by volume.
The coating system studied was a diffusion aluminide coating, Codep B-1, applied by the pack cementation process.
The coating microstructure consisted of an NiAl additive layer with embedded alpha Al2O3 particles, and a fingered diffusion zone with sigma phase, MC carbides, and NiAl.
